rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM music_Track;
rows.note: Assuming "tracks in the catalog" means all rows in music_Track.

rows.sql: SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(al.AlbumId) AS album_count FROM music_Artist ar JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name HAVING COUNT(al.AlbumId) = (SELECT MAX(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM music_Album GROUP BY ArtistId))
rows.note: Assuming "most albums" means the count of rows in music_Album per artist, with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT Country, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM music_Customer GROUP BY Country ORDER BY customer_count DESC, Country;
rows.note: Assumption: "music store" refers to the music_Customer table, grouped by its Country column.

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS year, ROUND(SUM(Total), 2) AS total_revenue FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY year ORDER BY year
rows.note: Assuming total revenue = sum of Invoice.Total grouped by calendar year of InvoiceDate.

rows.sql: SELECT c.FirstName || ' ' || c.LastName AS full_name, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS total_spent FROM music_Customer c JOIN music_Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.CustomerId, c.FirstName, c.LastName ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: Assumption: total spent is the sum of music_Invoice.Total per customer, with full name from music_Customer.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(c.CustomerId) AS CustomerCount
FROM music_Customer c
JOIN music_Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId, e.FirstName, e.LastName
HAVING COUNT(c.CustomerId) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM music_Customer WHERE SupportRepId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SupportRepId
  )
)
rows.note: Assuming "support rep" means music_Customer.SupportRepId, and I'll return all employees tied for the top count.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pt.TrackId) AS track_count FROM music_PlaylistTrack pt JOIN music_Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId WHERE p.Name = 'Grunge'
rows.note: Assuming the playlist is named exactly "Grunge" in music_Playlist and I count distinct tracks in music_PlaylistTrack.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS never_purchased_tracks FROM music_Track t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM music_InvoiceLine il WHERE il.TrackId = t.TrackId);
rows.note: Assuming "never purchased" means the track has no row in music_InvoiceLine.

rows.sql: SELECT BillingCountry, SUM(Total) AS Revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE InvoiceDate >= '2012-01-01' AND InvoiceDate < '2013-01-01' GROUP BY BillingCountry ORDER BY Revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: Assuming revenue is the sum of Invoice.Total for invoices dated in 2012, grouped by BillingCountry, returning only the top country.

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.Name AS ArtistName
FROM music_Artist ar
JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 3;
rows.note: Assuming "tracks" link to artists via Track → Album → Artist, counting distinct genres per artist.

rows.sql:
SELECT g.Name AS Genre,
ROUND(100.0 * SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) / (SELECT SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) FROM music_InvoiceLine), 2) AS Percentage
FROM music_InvoiceLine il
JOIN music_Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
JOIN music_Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
ORDER BY Percentage DESC
rows.note: I'll compute revenue per genre from invoice lines (UnitPrice × Quantity) and express each as a share of the total line revenue.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT i.CustomerId) AS customer_count
FROM music_Invoice i
JOIN music_InvoiceLine il ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
WHERE g.Name = 'Rock'
AND i.CustomerId NOT IN (
  SELECT i2.CustomerId
  FROM music_Invoice i2
  JOIN music_InvoiceLine il2 ON il2.InvoiceId = i2.InvoiceId
  JOIN music_Track t2 ON t2.TrackId = il2.TrackId
  JOIN music_Genre g2 ON g2.GenreId = t2.GenreId
  WHERE g2.Name = 'Jazz'
);
rows.note: I'll assume "bought" means the track appears on an invoice line, and genre is matched by music_Genre.Name ('Rock' / 'Jazz').

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, SUM(Total) AS revenue FROM music_Invoice WHERE strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2011' GROUP BY month ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll sum invoice Total by calendar month for 2011 and return the top month.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM music_Employee e WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM music_Customer c WHERE c.SupportRepId = e.EmployeeId)
rows.note: Assumption: "employees" refers to music_Employee, and a customer is assigned via music_Customer.SupportRepId.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_first_purchase_2010
FROM (
  SELECT CustomerId, MIN(InvoiceDate) AS first_purchase
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
) AS f
WHERE strftime('%Y', first_purchase) = '2010';
rows.note: Assuming "very first purchase" means each customer's earliest invoice date falls in 2010, I'll count distinct customers whose MIN(InvoiceDate) is in that year.

rows.sql: SELECT a.Title, ROUND(SUM(t.Milliseconds) / 60000.0, 1) AS minutes FROM music_Album a JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = a.AlbumId GROUP BY a.AlbumId, a.Title ORDER BY SUM(t.Milliseconds) DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: total running time is the sum of track Milliseconds per album, converted to minutes (ms / 60000).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, SUM(Total) AS revenue
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY yr
),
yoy AS (
  SELECT yr,
         ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
         ROUND((revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr)) * 100.0 / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY yr), 1) AS yoy_pct_change
  FROM yearly
)
SELECT yr, revenue, yoy_pct_change
FROM yoy
WHERE yr > (SELECT MIN(yr) FROM yearly)
ORDER BY yr
rows.note: You're right: the question asks only for years after the first, so I'll drop 2009.
rows.review: The result includes the first year (2009) with a NULL percentage, but the question asks only for years after the first. Filter out the first year, for example by wrapping the query and adding `WHERE yoy_pct_change IS NOT NULL` or `WHERE yr > (SELECT MIN(yr) FROM yearly)`.

rows.sql: WITH cust AS (SELECT CustomerId, SUM(Total) AS spend FROM music_Invoice GROUP BY CustomerId) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_above_avg FROM cust WHERE spend > (SELECT AVG(spend) FROM cust);
rows.note: I'll compare each customer's total invoice spend against the average per-customer spend, counting customers who appear in music_Invoice.

rows.sql:
WITH pa AS (
  SELECT pt.PlaylistId, COUNT(DISTINCT al.ArtistId) AS artist_count
  FROM music_PlaylistTrack pt
  JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = pt.TrackId
  JOIN music_Album al ON al.AlbumId = t.AlbumId
  GROUP BY pt.PlaylistId
)
SELECT p.Name, pa.artist_count
FROM pa
JOIN music_Playlist p ON p.PlaylistId = pa.PlaylistId
WHERE pa.artist_count = (SELECT MAX(artist_count) FROM pa);
rows.note: Assumption: artists are reached via Track → Album → Artist, and ties are all returned.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM (SELECT il.InvoiceId FROM music_InvoiceLine il JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId GROUP BY il.InvoiceId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.GenreId) > 1) sub;
rows.note: Assuming an invoice "contains tracks from more than one genre" when its invoice lines reference tracks with at least 2 distinct GenreIds.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS support_rep, SUM(i.Total) AS revenue_2010
FROM music_Invoice i
JOIN music_Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId
JOIN music_Employee e ON e.EmployeeId = c.SupportRepId
WHERE strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2010'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeId
HAVING SUM(i.Total) = (
  SELECT MAX(s) FROM (
    SELECT SUM(i2.Total) AS s
    FROM music_Invoice i2
    JOIN music_Customer c2 ON c2.CustomerId = i2.CustomerId
    WHERE strftime('%Y', i2.InvoiceDate) = '2010' AND c2.SupportRepId IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c2.SupportRepId
  )
);
rows.note: Assumption: "revenue" means the sum of `music_Invoice.Total` for invoices dated in 2010, grouped by each customer's support rep.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS year, g.Name AS genre,
         SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS revenue
  FROM music_InvoiceLine il
  JOIN music_Invoice i ON i.InvoiceId = il.InvoiceId
  JOIN music_Track t ON t.TrackId = il.TrackId
  JOIN music_Genre g ON g.GenreId = t.GenreId
  GROUP BY year, genre
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT year, genre, revenue,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
  FROM rev
)
SELECT year, genre, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 2
ORDER BY year;
rows.note: Assumption: revenue is SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity) from music_InvoiceLine, grouped by the invoice year and the track's genre, with ties at second place all shown.

rows.sql:
WITH y AS (
  SELECT CustomerId,
    SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS t2013,
    SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN Total ELSE 0 END) AS t2012
  FROM music_Invoice
  GROUP BY CustomerId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_2013_than_2012
FROM y
WHERE t2013 > t2012;
rows.note: Assuming "spent" means the sum of invoice Total per customer by calendar year (2012 and 2013), counting customers whose 2013 total exceeds their 2012 total (customers with no 2012 spend count as 0).

rows.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT Total, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY Total) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM music_Invoice
)
SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total
FROM ordered
WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2);
rows.note: Assuming the median is taken over all rows of music_Invoice.Total (averaging the two middle values when the count is even).

rows.sql:
SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
FROM music_Artist ar
JOIN music_Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
JOIN music_Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
JOIN music_PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) = (
  SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pt2.PlaylistId) AS cnt
    FROM music_Album al2
    JOIN music_Track t2 ON t2.AlbumId = al2.AlbumId
    JOIN music_PlaylistTrack pt2 ON pt2.TrackId = t2.TrackId
    GROUP BY al2.ArtistId
  )
);
rows.note: Assumption: count distinct playlists per artist via Track → Album → Artist, and return only the top artist(s).

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM music_InvoiceLine) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM music_Invoice), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice
rows.note: Assuming each InvoiceLine row is a line item and every invoice counts, including invoices with no lines (which contribute zero), I'll divide total line rows by total invoices.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS discontinued_products FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '1';
rows.note: Assuming Discontinued = '1' marks discontinued products.

rows.sql: SELECT CompanyName FROM shop_Suppliers WHERE Country = 'Germany'
rows.note: Assumption: "based in Germany" means the Country column of shop_Suppliers equals 'Germany'.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, COUNT(p.ProductID) AS ProductCount FROM shop_Categories c JOIN shop_Products p ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID GROUP BY c.CategoryID, c.CategoryName HAVING COUNT(p.ProductID) = (SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM shop_Products GROUP BY CategoryID))
rows.note: Assuming "most products" means the count of products in shop_Products per category, I'll return the top category (all ties included).

rows.sql: SELECT strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS Year, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount FROM shop_Orders GROUP BY Year ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: Assuming "placed" means OrderDate, grouped by calendar year from the shop_Orders table.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName AS shipper_name, ROUND(AVG(o.Freight), 2) AS avg_freight FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Shippers s ON o.ShipVia = s.ShipperID GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assumption: average freight is taken over all orders in shop_Orders, grouped by the shipper via ShipVia.

rows.sql: SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName FROM shop_Employees e WHERE e.ReportsTo = (SELECT EmployeeID FROM shop_Employees WHERE FirstName = 'Andrew' AND LastName = 'Fuller')
rows.note: Andrew Fuller is the shop_Employees row with FirstName 'Andrew' and LastName 'Fuller'; I'll find employees whose ReportsTo points to his EmployeeID.

rows.sql:
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, COUNT(*) AS OrderCount
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, FullName
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MAX(c) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM shop_Orders o2
    WHERE o2.OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND o2.OrderDate < '2021-01-01'
    GROUP BY o2.EmployeeID
  )
)
rows.note: Assumption: "handled" means the employee recorded on shop_Orders, counted by OrderDate in calendar year 2020.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE UnitPrice > (SELECT AVG(UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products);
rows.note: Assuming "average product unit price" means the average of UnitPrice across all rows in shop_Products.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_shipped_to_france FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShipCountry = 'France'
rows.note: Assuming "shipped to France" means ShipCountry = 'France' on shop_Orders, counting all orders regardless of whether ShippedDate is set.

rows.sql: SELECT p.ProductName, ROUND(SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID GROUP BY p.ProductID, p.ProductName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 5
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from the order details, grouped by product.

rows.sql: SELECT c.CategoryName, p.ProductName, p.UnitPrice FROM shop_Products p JOIN shop_Categories c ON p.CategoryID = c.CategoryID WHERE p.UnitPrice = (SELECT MAX(p2.UnitPrice) FROM shop_Products p2 WHERE p2.CategoryID = p.CategoryID) ORDER BY c.CategoryName
rows.note: Assuming "most expensive" means the highest UnitPrice within each category (ties all included).

rows.sql: SELECT c.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Customers c ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID JOIN "shop_Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2021-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2022-01-01' GROUP BY c.CustomerID, c.CompanyName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = SUM(UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount)) over order lines whose OrderDate falls in 2021, and return the top customer(s) by that total.

rows.sql: SELECT CAST(strftime('%m', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM "shop_Orders" WHERE strftime('%Y', OrderDate) = '2021' GROUP BY month ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assuming "orders" means rows in shop_Orders grouped by OrderDate month for year 2021.

rows.sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM shop_Orders o
  JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = o.EmployeeID
  WHERE o.OrderDate >= '1997-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '1998-01-01'
  GROUP BY e.EmployeeID, e.FirstName, e.LastName
)
SELECT EmployeeID, FirstName, LastName, n AS OrderCount FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c);
rows.note: The shop_Orders table has no orders from 1997. Its OrderDate values run only from 2012 through 2023, so no employee can be credited with 1997 orders.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_shipped_orders FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL AND ShippedDate > RequiredDate;
rows.note: Assuming "shipped after required date" means ShippedDate is not NULL and ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(ShippedDate) - julianday(OrderDate)), 1) AS avg_days FROM shop_Orders WHERE ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
rows.note: Assuming "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and the average is over the difference in days between ShippedDate and OrderDate.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM shop_Products WHERE Discontinued = '0' AND UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel;
rows.note: Assuming "still sold" means Discontinued = '0' and "below reorder level" means UnitsInStock < ReorderLevel.

rows.sql: SELECT c.Country, COUNT(o.OrderID) AS order_count FROM shop_Orders o JOIN shop_Customers c ON o.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2019-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2020-01-01' GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: Assumption: count orders by the customer's country (shop_Customers.Country) for orders with OrderDate in 2019.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.CategoryName = 'Beverages' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) / SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)), 1) AS beverages_pct FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN shop_Categories c ON c.CategoryID = p.CategoryID WHERE o.OrderDate >= '2023-01-01' AND o.OrderDate < '2024-01-01'
rows.note: I'll assume 2023 is based on OrderDate, revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), and the percentage is Beverages revenue divided by total 2023 revenue.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM shop_Orders WHERE OrderDate >= '2020-01-01' AND OrderDate < '2021-01-01' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT strftime('%m', OrderDate)) = 12) AS t;

WITH order_totals AS (
  SELECT o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID, SUM(d.UnitPrice * d.Quantity * (1 - d.Discount)) AS order_value
  FROM "shop_Orders" o
  JOIN "shop_Order Details" d ON d.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.OrderID, o.EmployeeID
),
emp_avg AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID, AVG(order_value) AS avg_order_value
  FROM order_totals
  GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name, ea.avg_order_value
FROM emp_avg ea
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = ea.EmployeeID
ORDER BY ea.avg_order_value DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'm treating each order's value as the sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its lines, then averaging those order values per employee and returning the top one.

rows.sql: SELECT s.CompanyName, SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue FROM "shop_Order Details" od JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = od.ProductID JOIN shop_Suppliers s ON s.SupplierID = p.SupplierID WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' GROUP BY s.SupplierID, s.CompanyName ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) from order details, with the order date in 2018 and grouped by supplier company name.

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2022
  FROM "shop_Order Details" od
  JOIN shop_Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT y.ProductID, p.ProductName, y.units_2021, y.units_2022,
         y.units_2022 - y.units_2021 AS increase
  FROM yearly y
  JOIN shop_Products p ON p.ProductID = y.ProductID
)
SELECT ProductID, ProductName, units_2021, units_2022, increase
FROM diff
WHERE increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM diff);
rows.note: Assumption: units sold is the sum of `Quantity` from Order Details, grouped by the calendar year of `OrderDate`, with a missing year counted as 0.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS shipper_name,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_late
FROM shop_Orders o
JOIN shop_Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "arrived after the required date" means ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT yr AS year, cnt AS orders_in_year, SUM(cnt) OVER (ORDER BY yr ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_orders FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM shop_Orders GROUP BY yr) ORDER BY yr
rows.note: Assumption: count orders per calendar year from OrderDate, then take a cumulative sum ordered by year.

rows.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_over_10000 FROM (SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total FROM "shop_Order Details" GROUP BY OrderID HAVING total > 10000) t
rows.note: Assuming total value per order = sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its line items, and "above 10,000" means strictly greater than 10,000.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID, strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) AS yr,
         SUM(od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount)) AS revenue
  FROM shop_Orders o
  JOIN "shop_Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) IN ('2018','2019')
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID, yr
),
pivot AS (
  SELECT EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr='2018' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN yr='2019' THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) AS rev2019
  FROM rev GROUP BY EmployeeID
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS full_name,
       p.rev2018, p.rev2019, (p.rev2019 - p.rev2018) AS growth
FROM pivot p
JOIN shop_Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = p.EmployeeID
ORDER BY growth DESC
LIMIT 1;
rows.note: I'll assume revenue = UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount), attributed to the order's EmployeeID, comparing calendar years 2018 and 2019, and return the employee with the largest absolute increase.
